kernelAudit.readAs: an anchored read in EITHER declared realm: `<alias>.<key>` inside the scope of a binding of the realm's own aliasPath, or a read through the WHOLE path. OverDex binds no alias and reads `fusion.kernelAudit.ok` directly, so an alias-only test credits nothing there.
kernelAudit.seededFrom: the anchored test above, hand-checked line by line on 2026-11-12. `integrator-app.js:78` and `:79` read `ka.mismatches`, `:80` reads `ka.expected`. `overdex-app.js:862` reads `fusion.kernelAudit.ok` and `:866` reads `.mismatches`. widenedRealm: 2026-11-12: depth 1 was judged against ONE file, so `export-only` — "carried on the node-export and deliberately not rendered" — was never asked of the app. `integrator-render.js` names neither `clockSkew` nor `kernelAudit`; `integrator-app.js` binds both (`var ka = FUSION && FUSION.kernelAudit` at :77, `var cs = FUSION && FUSION.clockSkew` at :88) and pushes a reader-facing banner line from each into `warnAll`. Both cells now read `card` against the app realm. The other 22 export-only keys stay: three of them match a bare token in the app and none reads the fusion, which is why a second realm is asked for an anchored read.
widenedNested: 2026-11-12 — `fusion.kernelAudit` is the third nested subtree judged, and the first read in more than one realm. `overdex-app.js` joins readerRealms with holder `fusion`, measured to move no depth-1 cell.
widenedElements: 2026-11-12 — depth 3. An element shape belongs to the BUILDER's element literal and not to the array key, so one `entry` shape serves `nodes[]` and `mismatches[]`. A member chain split across lines defeats a per-line regex: `overdex-app.js` writes the array on one line and `.map(` on the next, and a line-by-line scan reported that site as absent. The gate counts every element read it does not judge.
